title: Urgent payment or account warning
summary: Use these immediate steps when someone is pressuring you to pay, share a code, or approve access.
immediate_actions: Pause. Do not send money, approve a request, or share a one-time code.
Move away from the message or call and do not use its links or phone numbers.
If a bank, wallet, or account may be affected, contact that provider through an independently located channel.
preserve_evidence: Keep the original message, sender details, timestamps, receipts, and transaction references.
Do not edit or forward evidence if doing so could expose a password, PIN, or one-time code.
recovery_actions: Change affected credentials from a known-safe device and sign out other sessions where the provider supports it.
Ask the payment or account provider what containment and reversal options are available.
Monitor statements and account notices for further activity.
escalation_guidance: If there is immediate physical danger, use your device's emergency function or a local emergency service you already know.
Use an official reporting destination only after independently checking its source and destination.
A local trusted person can help preserve evidence and slow down further contact.

title: Possible account takeover
summary: Contain access changes without following instructions from the suspicious message.
immediate_actions: Stop responding and do not share a recovery code or approve an unexpected sign-in.
Open the provider's app or website using a known bookmark or manually entered address.
Check security alerts and active sessions from that trusted route.
preserve_evidence: Record the time, device, alert wording, and visible account changes.
Keep suspicious messages available for later reporting without opening additional links.
recovery_actions: Use the provider's account-recovery process and update credentials from a safe device.
Review recovery email addresses, phone numbers, payment methods, and active sessions.
Tell contacts through a trusted channel if the account may have sent messages without your control.
escalation_guidance: Contact the provider through its independently verified support path.
Ask a trusted person to help if you are being pressured or cannot distinguish a genuine alert.
